In [[mathematics]], '''Maillet's determinant''' ''D''<sub>''p''</sub> is the [[determinant]] of the [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] introduced by {{harvtxt|Maillet|1913}} whose entries are ''R''(''s/r'') for ''s'',''r'' = 1, 2, ..., (''p''&nbsp;–&nbsp;1)/2 ∈ '''Z'''/''p'''''Z''' for an odd prime ''p'', where  and ''R''(''a'') is the least positive residue of ''a'' [[modulo]] ''p'' {{harv|Muir|1930|loc=pages 340–342}}. 

==Determinant value==

{{harvtxt|Malo|1914}} calculated the determinant ''D''<sub>''p''</sub> for ''p''&nbsp;=&nbsp;3, 5, 7, 11, 13 and found that in these cases it is given by (–''p'')<sup>(''p''&nbsp;–&nbsp;3)/2</sup>, and conjectured that it is given by this formula in general. {{harvtxt|Carlitz|Olson|1955}} showed that this conjecture is incorrect; the determinant in general is given by ''D''<sub>''p''</sub> = (–''p'')<sup>(''p''&nbsp;–&nbsp;3)/2</sup>''h''<sup>−</sup>, where ''h''<sup>−</sup> is the first factor of the [[Ideal class group|class number]] of the [[cyclotomic field]] generated by ''p''th roots of 1, which happens to be 1 for ''p'' less than 23. In particular, this verifies Maillet's conjecture that the determinant is always non-zero. Chowla and Weil had previously found the same formula but did not publish it.
Their results have been extended to all non-prime odd numbers by {{harvtxt|Wang|1984}}.
